value.name: Daniel challenges the legal claim
value.description: Daniel argues that the speaker misread the situation and is not a lawyer, while invoking his mother's medications to dispute the implication.
evidence: "think you saw, but you are not a lawyer, and my mother was on three different medications by October, and —"

value.name: Asha orders Daniel to sit
value.description: Asha uses an authoritative tone to cut off Daniel and make him sit down.

value.name: Daniel suppresses his anger
value.description: Daniel obeys Asha's command but does so angrily, masking his fury with a hand over his face.
evidence: He sat down because Asha had used the voice she had been taught, in her first year of practice, by a judge who had told her that the only authority a young woman would ever have in a room of older men was the authority she took without asking.
He sat down, and he was furious about sitting down, and he covered the fury with a hand passed over his face.

value.name: Asha asks about the paper
value.description: Asha presses Rosa to explain what the document said.
evidence: "Rosa," Asha said. "What did the paper say."

value.name: Rosa describes the will change
value.description: Rosa says she did not read the paper carefully but was told it was a change to the señora's will concerning the house.
evidence: "I did not read it carefully. I am not the kind to read other people's papers. The señora told me it was a change to her will. She said the house was the question. She said she wanted to be sure."

value.name: Lawyer dictates and paper is signed
value.description: Rosa explains that another lawyer spoke by phone, the señora wrote and read the document aloud, and multiple people signed it.
evidence: "The lawyer, not Mr. Halloran but another man, was on the telephone. She wrote on a piece of paper. She read it aloud. She signed at the bottom. I signed. Mrs. Kim from across the street signed."

value.name: Document is stored in sewing room drawer
value.description: Rosa says the señora placed the signed paper in a folder and hid it in the bottom drawer of her desk in the sewing room.
evidence: "The señora put the paper in a folder and the folder in the bottom drawer of her desk in the sewing room."

value.name: Asha clarifies the sewing room
value.description: Asha identifies the sewing room as the small back room upstairs where the señora kept her machine and paid bills.
evidence: "The small room on the second floor at the back. Where she kept her machine. She did her bills there."
value.location_hint: small room on the second floor at the back

value.name: Asha asks whether the folder was searched
value.description: Asha asks Rosa if she has looked for the folder since the señora died.
evidence: "Have you looked for the folder since she died?"

value.name: Rosa refuses to search the house
value.description: Rosa says she has not looked for the folder because the house is not hers and she no longer works there.
evidence: "Because it is not my house," Rosa said, "and I am not employed here anymore."

value.name: Daniel ends Rosa's employment
value.description: Rosa reveals that Daniel told her last Friday her services would no longer be needed after the funeral.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano informed me last Friday that my services would not be required after the funeral."

value.name: Lucia summons Rosa to testify
value.description: Rosa says she came to the meeting because Miss Lucia asked her to come.
evidence: "I came today because Miss Lucia asked me to come."
